author: Nelev
body:
Both model calls and the record search were synchronous inside an `async def` handler, so one request held the event loop for its whole round trip and every other request queued behind it. Three concurrent conversations took as long as three sequential ones.

## Measured, against the running API

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| three concurrent requests | ~15s wall clock | **5s wall clock** (4.5s, 5.2s, 5.5s each) |
| 4001-character message | reached the model | **422**, before any model call |

## Async, not threaded

`AsyncOpenAI` for both rounds, awaited directly. A thread per in-flight call would also have worked — `asyncio.to_thread` was the first cut — but asyncio's default executor tops out around 32 workers, and that ceiling would become the concurrency limit on calls that take the better part of ten seconds each.

`search_record` follows: it awaits the embedding through a new `get_embedding_async`, and keeps **one** `to_thread` around the Chroma query. `PersistentClient` is embedded and synchronous, and `AsyncHttpClient` is for the client/server mode, so there is nothing to await there — it is a local HNSW search, but the thread keeps even that off the loop.

The sync embedding client stays for `rag_pipeline.run`, a script with no loop to await in. Both clients are `@lru_cache`d and lazy, so the server never constructs the one it does not use.

## Two limits

An unauthenticated endpoint that calls a billable API had neither:

- **Timeouts** — 45s on the model client, 20s on the embedding client. Without one the SDK waits indefinitely, and a hung upstream held the request, its database session and its worker until the client gave up. Note the SDK retries twice by default, so the worst case is roughly 3×.
- **`MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 4000`** on the message text. `min_length=1` with no ceiling meant the request body was the only limit on the prompt size, and the model bill paid for it.

## Also

Removes the nine tests for `POST /messages` and the `MessageRequest` import the endpoint's deletion left behind. Both were failing — `pytest` at 9 failures, `ruff` at 1 error — before this branch.

## Verified

`ruff format`, `ruff check` and **72 tests** pass. Live: `S5`, all three allergies named, 201 — the tool loop still behaves, now through the async client.

## Not in scope

Two findings from the same audit are untouched and still open: there is **no authentication anywhere** (`userId` is a query parameter, and the append endpoint has no ownership check), and a malformed `userId` still returns 500 rather than 422.
